title: An infinite finitely presented periodic group
main_claim: There is a finitely presented graded F2-algebra R=F2⊕I, infinite-dimensional, with every M_d(I) nil. For it, St_12(R) is infinite, finitely presented and periodic, and has property (T). As corollaries, I is a finitely presented nil but non-nilpotent algebra, and its unitization R is a finitely presented algebraic algebra (the finite-presentation versions of the Kurosh and Ufnarovskij questions).

issues.location: sec:finite-rules, transaction head format (zero task) / Lemma fr:faithful
issues.description: Soundness of zero-task verification depends on the format condition that a zero-task head always has committed side ε=0. If ε=1 were allowed, acquisition would put the represented data into slot 1 while slot 0 (the only slot tested) is arbitrary, and a forged zero success would become reachable from a clean word. The paper states 'For a zero task ε=0' as a head-format condition, and creation moves are restricted to admissible formats, so this appears covered. It is one of several low-level table conditions that are asserted rather than listed exhaustively.
issues.evidence: 'A head, and only a head, also carries a committed-side bit ε. For a zero task ε=0.' Creation: 'with chosen l,τ,ε'; move instances are taken 'subject to the syntactic formats'.

coverage:
Read all five sections in full.

K-theory and group half, checked line by line:
- The finite Steinberg presentation for n≥5. Verified the three-factor commutator lemma algebraically, the split-graph connectivity, the commutation induction, and both empty-word cases.
- The presentation of GL_n(R) by relations on at most five coordinates, via coset transport on the frame complex. Checked well-definedness, the triangle relation ststs=t, generation, and injectivity.
- Centrality of J_n for n≥6 via an action on strips.
- K1 stability.
- The bijection Hom(J_n,Q) ↔ H^2(E_n;Q), natural in rank.
- Matroid connectivity of the frame complex.
- Vanishing of the stabilizer columns. N_l = M_{l×r}(R)⋊S_l is locally finite, and a transposition kills the sign coinvariants. Then the E^1 spectral-sequence argument for H_2 stability at n≥12.
- Torsion of J_n(F2).
- Block-root laws and triangular faithfulness.
- Wrap removal: band widths, the opposite-root exclusion, and at most one endpoint move per block factor.
- Conjugating the unipotent cyclic shift C_N (N a power of two) to triangular form; W = ι_1(u)^N equals a product of ι_s(u(0)).
- Rational descent.

Algebra half, checked:
- The basis lemma for binomial/monomial presentations.
- Alternating-sum cancellation for m>d^2 in characteristic 2.
- The orbit/packet argument in direct cancellation: freeness of the orbit, invariance of the chosen run, discarding zero words.
- The exact cut-reduction identity.
- The automaton block identity and its dimension bound.
- The growth computation: 2kc/(D−1)<1 under D>10(c+1)(k+1).
- z-coefficient extraction showing T^a=0.
- Token normalization and the bound on fragments between cuts.
- Rollback and verification path logic.
- The palette checker.
- The Kleene fixed point and its time and size bounds: certificate O(T^2) ≤ 2^h, polynomial running time < T = 2^{h/5}.

Not checked: every individual entry of the finite rule table (exact field formats and move instances) beyond the stated lemmas.
sibling_notes: Sibling rank 344 (the residually finite 2-group paper) depends on this paper's Theorem algebra and its hierarchy. I found no gap in either: the hierarchy (Prop 2.2) and the cancellation/matrix-nil theorem look internally consistent. The K-theory half is independent of the companion and self-contained.
